terms.gloss: other; in the plural, others, other things
terms.grammar: adjective and pronoun; dat. aliī; for the genitive alterīus is usual
terms.comment: Other people are aliī, other things alia. “Other than” is alius nisi or alius ac: ab aliō nisi ab rēge (Gell. 5.2.3). The rest of a group already named are cēterī (see the others); of two, alter (see the other).

evidence: Publil. Sent. A 28: Aliēna nōbīs, nostra plūs aliīs placent.
terms.comment: Belonging to another, as against suus and noster: aliēna, other people’s things.

phrases.latin: prātēnsibus optima fungīs nātūra est; aliīs male crēditur
phrases.english: meadow mushrooms are the best by nature; the other kinds are not to be trusted

phrases.latin: prīsca juvent aliōs: ego mē nunc dēnique nātum grātulor
phrases.english: let the old days please others: I am glad I was born now

phrases.latin: Aliēna nōbīs, nostra plūs aliīs placent.
phrases.english: Other people’s things please us, and ours please others more.

phrases.latin: haud umquam īnscendī sēsē ab aliō nisi ab rēge passus sit
phrases.english: he never let anyone other than the king mount him

phrases.latin: olīvae betācei cucurbitae bulbī, alia mīlle nōn minus lauta
phrases.english: olives, beets, gourds, onions, a thousand other things no less fine

phrases.latin: hāc rē vidēre nostra mala nōn possumus; aliī simul dēlinquunt, cēnsōrēs sumus
phrases.english: that is why we cannot see our own faults; as soon as others go wrong, we are their censors

sources: Lewis & Short: alius · Lewis & Short: alienus
Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-horatius, loci-ovidius, loci-publilius, loci-gellius, loci-plinius, loci-phaedrus), checked against the editions named there.
Publilius is cited as the loci collection numbers him, by position under each initial letter in the Latin Library text; from N onwards that numbering differs from Meyer’s.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 355.
